newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil firms profits to be hit by poor market.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil firms profits to be hit by poor market.

text.p: Japanese oil firms' profits, already hit by surging crude prices in the first half of this business year, are expected to suffer from low prices for oil products in the second half, analysts said on Wednesday.
"Oil firms are expected to have a hard time achieving their profit forecasts for the full business year," said Toshinori Itoh, senior analyst at the Daiwa Institute of Research.
"They will most probably be forced to adjust their product prices to better reflect the retail market, and this move will depress profits," he said.
Leading oil firms, which in the past week have announced results for the six months to September 30, suffered steep falls in profits.
Industry giant Nippon Oil Co Ltd said its April-September parent company current profit plunged 86.8 percent against the same period last year to 946 million yen ($8.29 million).
Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd, another leading oil company, said its current profit in April-September amounted to two billion yen ($17.5 million), down 53 percent.
Current profits are pretax and include gains or losses on non-operating activities, such as investment in stocks.
The main reason for the slump in profits was a delay in passing on higher costs caused by a surge in global crude prices and the yen's weakness against the dollar to the wholesale price, they said.
The delay was due to the fact that Japanese refiners take into account the previous month's international crude oil and product prices to set the next month's domestic oil product wholesale prices.
For the full year, Nippon Oil forecast current profits of 12 billion yen ($105 million), up almost 10 percent from the last year's result.
Idemitsu's current profit forecast for the full year was 10 billion yen ($87.7 million), up 17.6 percent from 1995/96.
Analysts said oil firms would find it difficult to achieve their targets for a number of reasons, such as poor prospects of a recovery in the domestic retail price of oil products.

Dealerships have been hit by shrinking profit margins, and oil firms might have to provide financial assistance to those with which they have strong business ties, said Masaru Ohkawa, analyst with Nomura Research Institute.
Analysts also said that the rises in retail prices have not matched increases in wholesale prices.
This was because of cut-throat competition among petrol stations and also because truck drivers have opposed rises in the price of gas oil, which is used as fuel, they said.
Moreover, consumers have opposed efforts to raise the price of kerosene, used for heating in homes.
Daiwa's Itoh said many oil firms were expected to adjust their wholesale prices to support dealerships which bore the brunt of the effect of low retail prices so far this year.
"Oil firms should let the market decide prices. Ideally, prices should differ according to the region and according to the competition they face there," Itoh said.
Oil product wholesale prices, which oil firms set on a monthly basis after taking into account international crude prices and the currency market, are the same nationwide.

According to a survey by the Trade Ministry last month, Japan's 12 leading oil firms expect current profits for the whole of this business year to fall 32.5 percent to a combined 85 billion yen ($745 million). ($1=114 yen)
